verdict: Mostly trustworthy, and complete enough to hand to the team once a handful of framing fixes are applied. Every number in the front matter, section 9 and Appendix A recomputes exactly from _context.json, the baselines and items.verified.json (227 baseline records and their per-category status splits, tiers 24/45/27 to 23/42/31, verdicts 9/78/9, 29 effort revisions, statuses 68/21/4/3, reference check 24 items with 2 confirmed, 22 partial and 17 prevalence fixes, 1,505 records, 446 clusters, 144 candidates). The Priority table, all 96 wave-table rows (tier, effort, wave, 'was' markers) and all 96 card headers agree with _titles.json; every item sits in exactly one wave; the quick-win list matches the flags; and the ten ADR item lists match _context.json. The brief's six points are answered: table stakes (section 2), best of breed (section 3), differentiators and their benefit (section 7), separated nice-to-haves (section 6), three tiers, and a read-only audit framing. No blockers. The real problems are coherence slips where framing text kept pre-verification wording that the cards already corrected: headline 6 overstates prevalence ('all five') and calls attachments absent next to a Partial status; open question 3 re-opens the approval-resume question that section 1.5 declares answered; the F-t1-003/F-t1-004 plane columns and the F-t1-001 dependency repeat placements or a new Control decision that verification rejected; and Teams string evidence is tagged [REA] although Appendix A.3 says the strings were tokenizer-extracted, which overstates REA's role. The rest are minor: wording, a broken Appendix B cross-reference, a double-counted table-stakes row, the stray Apify mention, and undefined abbreviations.
